title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, Reliability Initiatives, Incident Reviews, Operational Tooling, and Runbooks
author: Ari Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning processes, reliability initiatives, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and canonical runbooks. It establishes measurable criteria, ownership, and required actions so teams can consistently operate services with predictable reliability and safe deployment practices.

Scope
Applies to all production-facing services owned by Redwood (hosted API, dedicated control-plane, serving runtime, telemetry services). Non-production environments should follow the same principles but use relaxed thresholds.

1) SLO framework and SLIs

Definition and goals
- SLI (Service Level Indicator): the telemetry signal that approximates user experience (e.g., successful responses, latency, error rates).
- SLO (Service Level Objective): the target for an SLI over a measurement window.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO over the measurement window; governs permissible failure/degredation.

Service tiers and recommended SLOs (table)
- Critical (user-facing inference path, customer SLA): availability 99.95% monthly; p99 latency < 300ms; error rate < 0.1%
- Core (control plane, model catalog, billing): availability 99.9% monthly; p99 latency < 500ms; error rate < 0.5%
- Non-critical (internal analytics, batch jobs): availability 99.0% monthly; p99 latency < 1s; error rate < 1%

Example SLO table (text representation)
- service_name: inference-api
  - SLI_type: successful_request_fraction
  - SLO: 99.95% (30-day window)
  - Error_budget: 0.05 (30-day window)
  - Measurement: Prometheus metric inference_requests{status!~"5.."}/inference_requests_total

SLI measurement sources and instrumentation
- Primary metrics: Prometheus (service-level counters, histograms), tracing (Tempo), logs (Loki) for post-facto causality.
- Derive SLI using production traffic only (filter out canary traffic via labels: environment=production, rollout_phase!=canary).

PromQL examples
- Successful request ratio (30m):
  rate_success = sum(rate(inference_requests_total{job="inference-api",status!~"5.."}[30m]))
  rate_total = sum(rate(inference_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[30m]))
  success_ratio = rate_success / rate_total

- 99th percentile latency (histogram_exemplar):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="inference-api"}[5m])) by (le))

2) Error budget policy & escalation

Burn rate policy (examples)
- Normal: burn rate < 1x - no action required.
- Elevated: burn rate >= 1x for 6 hours - SRE notified, product owner informed, initiate investigation.
- Constrained: burn rate >= 3x sustained for 1 hour or 2x for 24 hours - freeze non-critical releases, increase mitigation cadence.
- Emergency: burn rate >= 10x sustained for 1 hour - SEV1 incident process; immediate broad mitigations (traffic shaping, fallback to smaller model).

Escalation steps (numbered)
1. Pager/Slack alert triggers SRE rotation and oncall product owner.
2. Run initial triage (see runbook "Initial Triage: High Error Rate").
3. Determine whether to apply mitigations: throttle, circuit-break, rollback, route to fallback model or region.
4. If error budget consumption remains above threshold after mitigations, apply deployment freeze and launch root cause analysis (RCA) with timeline.
5. Communicate status to stakeholders with cadence (every 30 minutes for SEV1; hourly for SEV2).

Deployment controls linked to error budget
- When error budget is exhausted (0% remaining): automatic: block canary toggles; manual: require SRE signoff for any deploys to affected services.
- CI gating: PRs that modify request path must include an SLO impact assessment for critical services.

3) Capacity planning and runbook

Capacity model (core concepts)
- Demand signal: 95/99/99.9th percentile traffic in tokens/sec and requests/sec over 30/7/1-day windows.
- Safety buffer: maintain at least 20% spare capacity over forecasted 99th percentile under normal operations (configurable per service).
- Performance headroom: conservative GPU slot utilization target (e.g., 65% average, burst up to 85% for short windows).

Capacity planning process (quarterly and event-driven)
1. Gather inputs: business forecasts, marketing events, new-features rollouts, model changes (larger context length).
2. Telemetry collection: export request/tokens consumption per model and per region for last 90 days.
3. Run capacity simulation: scale requests against model performance curves (tokens/sec per GPU type).
4. Define required capacity and purchase/scale plan (dedicated pools, spot vs reserved).
5. Execute scaling and validate with staged load tests or blue-green traffic ramp.

Capacity runbook (quick steps)
- When latency SLO degradation is observed with no obvious upstream cause: 
  1) Verify autoscaling signals: pods, GPU pool health, pending pods, queue lengths.
  2) Check capacity dashboard: GPU utilization, model slot starvation, queue size.
  3) If starvation: increase pool size (Terraform runbook) or enable burst capacity policy for the pool.
  4) If sudden traffic spike: apply temporary rate-limiting at edge or shift traffic to lower-latency region.

Capacity calculation example (text)
- Inputs: target_peak_qps = 1200 req/s, avg_tokens_per_request = 200, model_tokens_per_second_per_gpu = 60000 tokens/s (throughput of quantized model on A10G)
- tokens_per_second = 1200 * 200 = 240,000 tokens/s
- required_gpus = ceil(240000 / 60000) = 4 GPUs + 20% buffer => 5 GPUs

4) Reliability initiatives and project governance

Quarterly reliability roadmap items (examples)
- Initiative: Prefix KV-cache for common prompt templates - reduce per-token compute by 12%. Owner: Runtime team. Target: Q3 2027.
- Initiative: Auto-fallback to small-model variant on 95th percentile tail - Owner: Serving runtime. Target: Q2 2027.
- Initiative: Reduce p99 latency by 20ms via kernel scheduling changes - Owner: Kernel/Scheduling. Target: next minor release.

Prioritization and measurement
- Each initiative must include success metrics (SLO improvement, cost delta), rollout plan, and experiment criteria. Track via quarterly reliability dashboards and measure impact on error budget consumption.

5) Incident review standards and postmortem template

Severity taxonomy
- SEV1: Service unavailable or severe customer impact (large outage of hosted API, breach of SLA).
- SEV2: Degraded service with significant customer impact (elevated error rates, higher latency affecting some customers).
- SEV3: Minor degradation, internal-only impact, or localized failures.

Postmortem template (required for SEV1/SEV2)
- Title
- SEV level
- Incident start/end timestamps (UTC)
- Summary (executive one-paragraph)
- Impact (customers affected, percentage of traffic, key metrics)
- Root cause (technical and human factors)
- Timeline of events (30-minute buckets for SEV1; 1-hour buckets for SEV2)
- Mitigations and immediate fixes
- Long-term action items (owner + due date)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups
- Evidence and links (graphs, traces, logs)

Review cadence
- Postmortem draft due within 72 hours of incident resolution.
- 1-week, 30-day follow-ups to verify action items.
- Dedicated reliability review board meets weekly to triage outstanding action items.

6) Operational tooling and monitoring stack

Canonical stack
- Metrics: Prometheus + Thanos for long-term retention.
- Alerting: Prometheus Alertmanager integrated with PagerDuty and SLO burn alerts.
- Dashboards: Grafana with per-service SLO panels, error budget panels, and cost-to-serve panels.
- Tracing: Tempo (distributed traces) linked into Grafana panels.
- Logs: Loki with structured JSON logs for request and model-level events.

Sample PrometheusRule (alert)
```
groups:
- name: inference-api.rules
  rules:
  - alert: InferenceApiHighErrorRate
    expr: |
      (sum(rate(inference_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m]))
       / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\"}[5m]))) > 0.005
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: page
    annotations:
      summary: \"inference-api error rate > 0.5% (5m)\"
      runbook: \"confluence/eng-sre/initial-triage-high-error-rate\"
```

SLO burn-rate alerting (recommended)
- Alert when burn rate >= 2x for 30 minutes (pager) and >= 4x for 1h (SEV1). Implement burn-rate calculation in a recording rule to avoid repeated heavy queries.

Operational automation examples
- Runbooks callable via Playbook CLI: `redwood runbook execute inference-api/scale-pool --size 2`
- Automated rollback: CI step can trigger `kubectl rollout undo` if a deployment canary exceeds error thresholds.

7) Canonical SRE runbooks (examples)

Runbook: Initial Triage - High Error Rate (inference-api)
- Trigger: Alert InferenceApiHighErrorRate fires.
- Owner: SRE oncall + service owner.
- Steps:
  1) Acknowledge alert and create a live incident channel (#inc-inference-api or Slack huddle).
  2) Run health checks:
     - curl -sS https://inference-api.internal.health/health || echo \"service down\"
     - kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --selector app=inference-api
     - kubectl describe pod <pod> (inspect recent restarts)
  3) Check metrics:
     - Grafana panel: inference-api / Errors / Error-rate (5m, 30m, 1h)
     - Prometheus query: (sum(rate(inference_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\",status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{job=\"inference-api\"}[5m])))
  4) Identify scope: global, region, customer subset (check request logs with label customer_id).
  5) Mitigation options (choose in order of least customer-impacting):
     - Re-route traffic to healthy region: `trafficctl shift inference-api --from us-west-2 --to eu-west-1 --percent 30`
     - Enable fallback small-model: `feature-flag-client set inference-api.fallback_small_model true --env=prod`
     - Scale GPU pool: `terraform apply -var='pool_size=+2'` or `redwood infra scale-gpu-pool --pool inference-prod --count 2`
     - Rollback last deployment: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-api`
  6) If mitigated, monitor error budget burn and confirm full recovery before ending incident.
  7) Draft postmortem following template.

Runbook: Capacity Spike - Queue Lengths Rising
- Trigger: queue_length > 2000 for 10 minutes and GPU queue pending pods > 50
- Steps:
  1) Increase autoscaler target: `kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-worker --replicas=10`
  2) Increase GPU pool burst: `redwood infra enable-burst --pool inference-prod --minutes 20`
  3) Enable rate limit on API edge for anonymous users: set header-based throttling rule in API gateway.
  4) Open load-test channel and run smoke validation against a canary region.

8) Ownership, runbook maintenance, and governance

- Ownership: Each service owning an SLO must list an SLO owner (engineer) and an SLO approver (team lead). The SRE team is the custodian of SLO policy and the enforcement automation.
- Review cadence: Every SLO and critical runbook reviewed quarterly. Document review recorded in Confluence comments and reviewers list.
- Runbook lifecycle: Runbooks must have a last-validation timestamp and smoke-tested at least once per quarter (game-day or simulated failure).
